title: Retention Composer for Query Artifacts with Attested Archive Webhooks
creator: Marin Chen
description:
Problem: Customers need a compact, auditable way to define retention for prompts, responses, request logs and metrics that supports per-route overrides, scheduled archival, and automated attested exports to downstream legal/compliance systems. Current retention controls are inflexible (route-wide TTLs and manual evidence exports) and create operational friction for compliance teams in regulated customers.

Goal: Deliver a Retention Composer UX + backend that lets tenants author composable retention policies (route prescriptive presets + conditionals), schedule attested evidence bundles, and trigger webhook-based archival or long-term storage flows. The feature must support per-route overrides, sampling rules for high-volume routes, region-aware residency constraints, and an attestation header/proof that downstream systems can record.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement HSM-backed signing for attestation (separate security work) and will not include on-prem installer changes for air-gapped exports in initial rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Console UX: A Retention Composer panel where PMs/Security can create named retention presets with TTL, sampling rate, and residency constraints; presets can be applied to a specific route or route group.
API: A retention policy API (CRUD) per tenant that returns effective policy for a route (respecting inheritance and overrides).
Archival hooks: Ability to register webhook endpoints for attested evidence exports; webhook payloads include signed metadata (policy id, timestamp, hash of included artifacts, residency provenance).
Scheduling: Policies support scheduled snapshots (daily/weekly) with optional delta mode for high-volume routes to reduce export size.
Sampling: Sampling configuration supports deterministic hashing by request id and percent-based sampling thresholds per route.
Residency constraints: Policies validate target archival location against tenant residency constraints and refuse mismatches in UI and API.
Audit trail: Each policy change is stored in an immutable change log with user, timestamp, and reason; change log is queryable via Console and API for at least 90 days.
E2E test: Integration test that creates a policy, sends sampled requests, triggers a scheduled export, and verifies webhook payload integrity (hash and metadata).
Docs: Console help text and API spec added to devdocs with examples for common compliance patterns.
proposed_solution: Add a policy service backed by retention-graph records (flat entries for route -> preset links) and a scheduler service that composes snapshot bundles. The scheduler will produce evidence bundles and call registered webhook endpoints with attestation metadata. UI will add a Retention Composer that maps presets to routes and validates residency constraints via existing tenant metadata service.
milestones: M1: API and data model for policies (2 weeks)
M2: Console Composer UI + validation (2 weeks)
M3: Scheduler + webhook exporter prototype (2 weeks)
M4: Sampling/delta export improvements + e2e tests (1 week)
M5: Documentation, security review, and launch (1 week)
metrics: Average export size reduction for sampled/delta exports (target >= 60%)
Number of tenants using per-route retention presets (target 10 pilot tenants in Q1)
Incidents caused by retention misconfiguration (target 0 post-launch)
risks_and_mitigations: Large-volume exports could overload downstream systems - mitigate with sampling, delta mode, and backpressure + retry logic on webhook sender.
Residency mismatch errors could block exports - mitigate by surfacing strong validation and preflight checks in the Console and API.
Evidence tampering concerns - mitigate by including signed hashes and later integrating HSM signing (follow-up security ticket).
Policy complexity could confuse users - mitigate with opinionated presets and a guided wizard in the Composer UX.
implementation_notes: Storage for bundles will reuse the existing evidence-s3 bucket with per-tenant prefixes and region tagging. Use existing tenant metadata endpoints to resolve residency. Scheduler must expose backpressure metrics to avoid runaway export load. Webhook sender should use idempotency keys derived from snapshot ids.
